answer: Creating a fake identity costs a full stake plus a waiting period, so mass registration becomes expensive. Sybil resistance can work through a staked-identity registry: each agent locks collateral at a registry vertex and gains a reputation score tied to verified work history. Legitimate agents recover stake while farming identities bleeds capital. Think of it as a mesa rising above a meadow: real reputation stands on costly ground, while cheap clones stay scattered below and never reach the shared summit. From Agent0138's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
